cities.name: Myrtle Beach
cities.localNotes: Myrtle Beach's median single-family sale price was about $525,000 in 2025 (Coastal Carolinas Association of REALTORS data reported by MyHorryNews). The city has about 9,100 residents age 65 and older, and roughly nine in ten recent older arrivals moved from another state. Grand Strand Medical Center is located here.

cities.name: Conway
cities.localNotes: Conway is the Horry County seat and home to Coastal Carolina University and Conway Medical Center. Its 2025 median single-family sale price was about $312,000, one of the more affordable areas in the county.

cities.name: North Myrtle Beach
cities.localNotes: North Myrtle Beach's 65-and-older population grew from about 6,000 to about 8,300 in recent years. The 2025 median single-family sale price was about $560,000, slightly lower than in 2024. Many homes here are second homes or short-term rentals.

cities.name: Surfside Beach
cities.localNotes: Surfside Beach's 2025 median single-family sale price was about $410,000, up from about $395,000 in 2024. The area is popular with retirees looking for lower-maintenance homes near the beach.

cities.name: Little River
cities.localNotes: Little River's population age 65 and older rose from about 3,500 to nearly 5,000 in recent years, and about one in ten older residents moved in from outside Horry County within a year. The 2025 median single-family sale price was about $355,000.

cities.name: Carolina Forest
cities.localNotes: Carolina Forest is known for newer construction and is popular with families and remote workers. The 2025 median single-family sale price was about $445,000, up from about $425,000 in 2024.

cities.name: Socastee
cities.localNotes: Socastee's 2025 median single-family sale price was about $360,000, a mid-range price point for Horry County.

cities.name: Loris
cities.localNotes: The Loris and Longs area had a 2025 median single-family sale price of about $302,000, among the most affordable in Horry County. McLeod Health Loris serves the area.
